title: Trusting an LLM judge blindly?

source.name: Netflix TechBlog
source.title: The Lifecycle of LLM-as-a-Judge: Building, Aligning, and Monitoring at scale

description: Netflix engineers wrote about building, aligning and monitoring an LLM judge at scale. The meme version.

scenes.narration: You use an LLM to grade your LLM. Who grades the grader?
scenes.headline: Who grades the grader?

scenes.narration: Netflix's engineering blog covers the full lifecycle of an LLM as a judge: building it, aligning it, and monitoring it at scale.
scenes.headline: The judge has a lifecycle

visual.top_text: Ship the judge, trust the scores
visual.bottom_text: Compare it to human labels first

scenes.narration: In plain terms, a judge is only useful if you keep checking it. Build it, align it, then keep monitoring it.
scenes.headline: Judge checklist

scenes.narration: Otherwise your dashboard is green and your product is quietly getting worse.
scenes.headline: Green dashboard, bad product

scenes.narration: My take: treat the judge like any model that can drift. Would you trust one with no human spot checks?
scenes.headline: Trust a judge with no spot checks?
